target.title: improve(imessage): manage imsg setup and plugin skill ownership
target.body:
Related: openclaw/imsg#157

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where OpenClaw's bundled iMessage guidance and setup flow lagged the current `imsg` CLI: the OpenClaw copy of the `imsg` skill still lived outside the iMessage plugin, did not document the landed poll behavior, and setup only reported that `imsg` was missing without offering the Homebrew install/update path most local Mac users need.

This is AI-assisted work.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `imsg` skill now lives with the bundled iMessage plugin, matching the existing Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, and QQBot channel-plugin pattern. The old top-level `skills/imsg` copy was removed.

The iMessage setup flow borrows the Signal-style prepare hook to offer macOS Homebrew install/update for the default local `imsg` path, while preserving explicit custom `cliPath` values, including SSH/PATH wrappers. Probe and setup status messages now distinguish default/Homebrew-managed `imsg` from operator-owned wrappers, and doctor can repair stale session snapshot paths to the generated plugin-skill path when that path has been published.

Clanker checked the prior Vincent/Jason history: Vincent previously moved bundled skills into plugin directories with manifest `skills` entries and did not add extra doctor migration. This PR keeps that ownership move, with a conservative doctor repair only for stale session metadata when the generated plugin-skill target exists.

Codex review note: local Codex review repeatedly flagged that moving `imsg` into plugin skills means the skill is only published when the iMessage plugin is activated. I am keeping that behavior because Omar explicitly asked to remove the old skill and align with other channel plugins; the PR body calls out the tradeoff for maintainer review.

## User Impact

Users configuring iMessage on the signed-in Messages Mac can install or update `imsg` from setup instead of manually discovering the command. Existing custom wrapper/SSH setups are left untouched, and setup/probe errors point operators at the configured wrapper when that is what is missing.

Agents using the iMessage skill get updated poll guidance, including the landed `imsg poll send` caption behavior and poll history/watch backfill notes.

target.title: fix(discord): disable ws 8.21.0 receiver part limits for gateway sockets
target.body:
## Summary

ws 8.21.0 introduced `maxBufferedChunks` and `maxFragments` receiver limits (commit `[security] Limit retained message parts`) that can trigger `WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS` and close connections with code 1008 under certain traffic patterns.

This PR explicitly sets both limits to `0` (disabled) for Discord gateway WebSocket connections, restoring the ws 8.20.0 behavior for the trusted Discord gateway peer while preserving the security fix for all other WebSocket usage.

## Changes

- **`extensions/discord/src/internal/gateway.ts`**: Base class `createWebSocket()` now passes `maxBufferedChunks: 0, maxFragments: 0` with a `ws.ClientOptions` cast (since `@types/ws` 8.18.1 does not yet expose these fields).
- **`extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-plugin.ts`**: Extended `DiscordGatewayWebSocketCtor` type to include the new options; monitor gateway creation path passes the same disabled limits.
- **`extensions/discord/src/internal/gateway.test.ts`**: Added test verifying base class WebSocket receives the expected options.
- **`extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-plugin.test.ts`**: Added test verifying monitor plugin WebSocket receives the expected options.
- **`extensions/discord/src/monitor/provider.proxy.test.ts`**: Updated two existing exact-match assertions to include the new options.

## Why `0` instead of raising the limits

- ws 8.21.0 treats `0` as disabled (`receiver.js:61`, `receiver.js:98`: `if (this._maxBufferedChunks > 0 && ...)`), matching the pre-8.21.0 behavior exactly.
- Discord gateway is a trusted peer; the security limits are designed to protect against untrusted senders.
- Choosing an arbitrary higher threshold would be fragile without real production traffic data to calibrate against.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: ws 8.21.0's retained-part receiver limits (`maxFragments` default 131072 / `maxBufferedChunks` default 1048576) abort a Discord gateway socket with `WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS` / close `1008`; this PR sets both to `0` (disabled) on the Discord gateway sockets, restoring ws 8.20.0 behavior for that trusted peer.
- **Real environment tested**: Live Discord gateway connection from a Docker `node:22-bookworm-slim` container (Node `v22.22.3`) with the repo-pinned `ws@8.21.0` installed exactly, using a real bot token (redacted), connecting to `wss://gateway.discord.gg/?v=10&encoding=json`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: build a `node:22-bookworm-slim` image with `npm install ws@8.21.0`, then run a client that constructs the gateway socket with this patch's options (`new ws.WebSocket(url, { handshakeTimeout: 30000, maxBufferedChunks: 0, maxFragments: 0 })`), completes the HELLO/IDENTIFY/READY handshake against the real Discord gateway, sends heartbeats, holds a 60s stable window, then closes with code 1000.
- **Evidence after fix**: Live Discord gateway run with this patch's options applied (token, `session_id`, and `resume_gateway_url` redacted):

```
[env] node=v22.22.3 ws=8.21.0
[discord] connecting wss://gateway.discord.gg (maxBufferedChunks:0, maxFragments:0)
[discord] open
[discord] HELLO heartbeat_interval=41250ms
[discord] IDENTIFY sent (token redacted)
[discord] READY received (session_id/resume_gateway_url redacted)
[discord] HEARTBEAT_ACK #1
[discord] stable window 60000ms complete
[discord] close code=1000 reason=<empty>
[result] PASS live: READY + 1 heartbeat ACK; no WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS during stable window
```

Supplemental deterministic mechanism repro against a local ws 8.21.0 gateway streaming one message in 131073 fragments (one over the client default `maxFragments`), exercising the same `ws.WebSocket` receiver path:

```
# default ws.WebSocket (ws 8.21 defaults)
[before] open
[before] error code=WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS message=Too many message fragments
[before] close code=1006 reason=<empty>

# this patch's options applied
[after] open
[after] message received: 131073 bytes - NO receiver-limit close
```

- **Observed result after fix**: On the real Discord gateway, with the disabled limits applied, the connection reaches `READY`, exchanges heartbeats, and stays connected through the 60s window with no `WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS` and no `1008` close; the only close is the intentional client-initiated `1000`. The deterministic repro confirms the same constructor options remove the receiver-limit close that the default ws 8.21 client hits.
- **What was not tested**: the live run confirms a real gateway session stays healthy with the patched options, but does not force Discord's production fragmentation pattern on demand, does not exercise the `zlib-stream` transport, and does not drive the full OpenClaw plugin wiring end-to-end. The deterministic repro proves the ws 8.21 retained-part mechanism and that this patch's options disable the exact receiver checks, but uses a local peer rather than Discord's live framing.

## Tests

- `gateway.test.ts`: 25 passed
- `gateway-plugin.test.ts`: 17 passed  
- `provider.proxy.test.ts`: 21 passed
- TypeScript check (tsgo): clean

Fixes #88330

target.title: feat(agents): per-agent outbound A2A allowlist override
target.body:
## Summary

- Add `agents.list[].tools.agentToAgent.allow` to control which agents a specific agent may contact via session tools (`sessions_send`, `sessions_list`, `sessions_history`, `session_status`)
- When unset, the agent falls back to the global `tools.agentToAgent.allow` list; when set to explicit IDs, only those targets are reachable; `[]` isolates the agent from all cross-agent access
- The global `tools.agentToAgent.allow` continues to act as a participation gate (both requester and target must match it) before per-agent outbound rules are evaluated
- Outbound-only semantics: only the requester's override is checked, not the target's
- Replace `matchesAllow` with `matchesGlobalParticipation` and add `evaluateAccess()` returning a structured `AgentToAgentDenyReason` so all call sites produce context-aware error messages via `formatAgentToAgentAccessError()`
- Scrub deleted agent references from per-agent outbound allowlists in `pruneAgentConfig()`

### Example config (hub-spoke pattern)

```json
{
  "tools": {
    "agentToAgent": { "enabled": true, "allow": ["*"] }
  },
  "agents": {
    "list": [
      { "id": "david",  "tools": { "agentToAgent": { "allow": ["*"] } } },
      { "id": "spoke",  "tools": { "agentToAgent": { "allow": ["david"] } } },
      { "id": "kelly",  "tools": { "agentToAgent": { "allow": ["david"] } } }
    ]
  }
}
```

spoke→david ✅ | spoke→kelly ❌ | david→anyone ✅

## Test plan

- [x] `sessions-access.test.ts`: per-agent override, deny-all `[]`, global gate, target override ignored (outbound-only), fallback to global when unset
- [x] `sessions.test.ts`: per-agent outbound deny during label lookup in `sessions_send`
- [x] `openclaw-tools.session-status.test.ts`: per-agent outbound deny for cross-agent `session_status`
- [x] `agents.test.ts`: `pruneAgentConfig` scrubs deleted agent from per-agent allowlists
- [x] Build passes
- [x] Manual: configure hub-spoke agents (david/spoke/kelly), verify per-agent outbound rules — see `Real behavior proof` section below

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: per-agent outbound `agentToAgent.allow` correctly gates cross-agent session tool access. Hub-spoke topology used: `david` (hub, `allow=["*"]`), `spoke` (allow=`["david"]`), `kelly` (allow=`["david"]`). Validates the new `evaluateAccess()` decision pipeline reaches the documented per-agent outbound semantics, with the structured `per_agent_outbound` deny reason surfaced via `formatAgentToAgentAccessError()`.

- **Real environment tested**: Ubuntu 22.04 (kernel 5.15), Node 22.22.0, pnpm 10. Branch HEAD `55819f6f43` of `repair/pr-39102-a2a-refresh` (this PR rebased on current main). Live invocation of the production export `createAgentToAgentPolicy` from `src/plugin-sdk/session-visibility.ts` — no mocks, no test runner, the same code path that backs `sessions_send`, `sessions_list`, `sessions_history`, and `session_status` at runtime.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

  1. Author a hub-spoke `OpenClawConfig` matching the docs example (david hub + spoke + kelly).
  2. Build `policy = createAgentToAgentPolicy(cfg)`.
  3. Call `policy.evaluateAccess(requester, target)` for the five edge pairs.
  4. Run with: `pnpm tsx proof-hub-spoke.ts` (the script imports the worktree source directly so the running code is the patched export).

- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output, copied verbatim from `node` stdout via `tsx`.

  ```
  # per-agent A2A allowlist — hub-spoke proof
  # config: david=hub (allow *), spoke=spoke (allow david), kelly=spoke (allow david)

  [ok ] spoke -> david: ALLOWED
  [ok ] spoke -> kelly: DENIED (reason=per_agent_outbound)
  [ok ] david -> kelly: ALLOWED
  [ok ] david -> spoke: ALLOWED
  [ok ] kelly -> spoke: DENIED (reason=per_agent_outbound)

  all cases match expected behavior
  ```

- **Observed result after fix**: all five real invocations matched the documented hub-spoke semantics. Cross-spoke calls (`spoke -> kelly`, `kelly -> spoke`) were denied with the structured `per_agent_outbound` reason code from `AgentToAgentDecision`. Hub-rooted calls (`david -> spoke`, `david -> kelly`) and spoke-to-hub (`spoke -> david`) were allowed. Process exit code: `0`. Console output above is the literal stdout, no post-processing.

- **What was not tested**: end-to-end IPC roundtrip through the live `sessions_send` agent process pair (single-machine ACP transport). The four session call sites all delegate the access decision to the single `evaluateAccess()` policy proven above, and the wiring of each call site is covered by the unit tests already listed in the Test plan.

target.title: Gateway: allow extension origins in browser allowlist
target.body: ## Summary Describe the problem and fix in 2–5 bullets: - Problem: `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` could not explicitly allowlist `chrome-extension://` because the origin checker normalized extension origins through `URL.origin`, which becomes `"null"` for that scheme. - Why it matters: extension sidepanel clients had to rely on `["*"]` to get through browser-origin WS checks, which weakened the intended hardening. - What changed: the origin matcher now keeps exact URL parsing/validation but falls back to exact `scheme://host` matching for non-standard origins, so `chrome-extension://` can be allowlisted exactly; focused unit and handshake tests were added. - What did NOT change (scope boundary): no wildcard/prefix expansion, no acceptance of literal `Origin: null`, no changes to token/device auth, host-header fallback, or non-browser client auth behavior. ## Change Type (select all) - [x] Bug fix - [ ] Feature - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Docs - [x] Security hardening - [ ] Chore/infra ## Scope (select all touched areas) - [x] Gateway / orchestration - [x] Auth / tokens - [ ] Memory / storage - [ ] Integrations - [ ] API / contracts - [ ] UI / DX - [ ] CI/CD / infra ## Linked Issue/PR - Closes #35035 (issue mentions app://* origin, but it's the same underlying problem) - Related #35396, #35057 (both PRS were fixes for this problem but were closed because the authors were banned AFAIK) ## User-visible / Behavior Changes - `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` can now contain exact extension origins such as `chrome-extension://abcdefghijklmnop`, and those browser-origin Gateway WS connects will succeed when otherwise authenticated. - Operators no longer need `["*"]` solely to let a Chrome extension sidepanel client connect. - Existing exact matches for normal `http(s)` origins, wildcard behavior, host-header fallback, and literal `Origin: null` rejection remain unchanged. ## Security Impact (required) - New permissions/capabilities? `No` (strictly speaking this allows chrome extensions/electron+tauri apps to connect but I think calling it a new capability is a stretch) - Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No` - New/changed network calls? `No` - Command/tool execution surface changed? `No` - Data access scope changed? `No` - If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: `N/A` ## Repro + Verification ### Environment - OS: macOS - Runtime/container: local Bun + Vitest - Model/provider: N/A - Integration/channel (if any): Gateway WS browser-origin client; Chrome extension origin emulated in handshake tests via `ws` - Relevant config (redacted): `gateway.auth.mode="token"`, `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins=["chrome-extension://abcdefghijklmnop"]` ### Steps 1. target.title: fix(web): avoid exact-limit fetch truncation warnings
target.body:
﻿Closes #101837

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `web_fetch` could see a response reported as truncated when the streamed response body was exactly `maxResponseBytes` bytes, even though no bytes were omitted.

## Why This Change Was Made

`readResponseText` now treats truncation as proven only when a chunk exceeds the remaining byte budget. Reaching the byte budget exactly no longer flips the truncation flag by itself, so exact-limit responses can complete normally while true overflow still cancels the reader.

## User Impact

Users no longer get misleading `Response body truncated after ... bytes.` warnings for complete responses that happen to land exactly on the byte cap. Oversized responses are still bounded and marked truncated.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: Current head `18b610b93e7e0a96de0eb891de3bab0e43f2c74b` lets an exact-limit `readResponseText` helper run complete without setting `truncated`, while still reporting the exact byte count.
- Real helper proof for the requested boundary, constructing a real `Response` from streamed chunks `"hello"` + `" world"` and reading it with `maxBytes: 11`:
  ```text
  node --import ../openclaw/node_modules/tsx/dist/esm/index.mjs --input-type=module -e "import { readResponseText } from './src/agents/tools/web-shared.ts'; const encoder = new TextEncoder(); let cancelCount = 0; const response = new Response(new ReadableStream({ start(controller) { controller.enqueue(encoder.encode('hello')); controller.enqueue(encoder.encode(' world')); controller.close(); }, cancel() { cancelCount += 1; } })); const result = await readResponseText(response, { maxBytes: 11 }); console.log(JSON.stringify({ text: result.text, truncated: result.truncated, bytesRead: result.bytesRead, cancelCount }));"
  {"text":"hello world","truncated":false,"bytesRead":11,"cancelCount":0}
  ```
- Focused regression: `PNPM_CONFIG_MODULES_DIR='../openclaw/node_modules' node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/web-shared.test.ts` passed (`1` file, `12` tests).
- Whitespace check: `git diff --check` passed.
- GitHub current-head checks: `gh pr checks 101845 --repo openclaw/openclaw --json name,bucket,state,completedAt,link` showed no failed buckets; current checks are pass/skip/neutral.
- Duplicate search before issue creation: no open issue or PR found for `web_fetch truncated maxBytes exact limit` or `readResponseText truncated maxBytes`.

Observed result: exact-limit helper output is `truncated:false`, `bytesRead:11`, and `cancelCount:0`, so the shared helper no longer feeds a false truncation warning to `web_fetch` for complete exact-cap responses.

target.title: Add reset family carryover summaries
target.body:
## Behavior or issue addressed

Depends on #90239.

When a session has been reset/rotated, the active transcript can be clean while the previous reset archive still contains the latest compaction summary. The next embedded-agent prompt therefore starts without the carryover context unless the model/tool explicitly asks for family history.

This change reuses the session-family transcript resolver from #90239 and injects the latest reset-archive compaction summary into embedded-agent prompt context before the LLM boundary, but only when the active context does not already contain a compaction summary.

## Fix

- Move the #90239 family/reset transcript target resolver into a shared gateway helper.
- Keep `chat.history(includeFamily)` on the shared resolver.
- Pass the current session store path/entry into embedded-agent attempts.
- Add a prompt-context transform that prepends one `compactionSummary` from reset ancestor transcripts.
- Skip injection when the active session already has a compaction summary.
- Cap family transcript read targets before reading files; ancestor targets stop at the cap while current-session targets remain available.
- Rebased onto current `origin/main` and preserved the newer transcript-reader seam plus same-session reset fallback.

## Real behavior proof

**Current head proven:** `ba74ecd54e52c2416ab8f7906491266b989f529c`.

**Behavior or issue addressed:** A reset/rotated logical session should read bounded reset-family history through the shared resolver, keep current reset archive plus current active transcript available inside the cap, preserve the newest eligible ancestors even when an older retained ancestor has many reset-topic archives, and inject exactly one reset-family compaction summary before the embedded-agent LLM boundary.

**Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw checkout on this PR branch at `/home/clever/.openclaw/workspace/github/openclaw`, using current branch TypeScript modules and temporary on-disk session stores/transcripts under `/tmp/openclaw-family-proof-ba74ecd54e-*`. No private channel, endpoint, phone, prompt, auth, or user transcript data was used.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
$ git rev-parse HEAD
ba74ecd54e52c2416ab8f7906491266b989f529c

$ node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'TS'

# - ./src/gateway/session-history-family.ts
# - ./src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/session-family-carryover.ts
# It created a temporary sessions.json, 35 ancestor transcripts,
# 35 owned reset-topic archives for ancestor 05, one current reset archive,
# and one current active transcript. It called the real family target resolver,
# real carryover resolver, installed the prompt transform, applied the transform
# twice, printed the observed result, and removed temp files.
TS
{
  "head": "ba74ecd54e52c2416ab8f7906491266b989f529c",
  "targetCount": 32,
  "firstTargets": [
    "ancestor-proof-05:ancestor-active:ancestor-proof-05.jsonl",
    "ancestor-proof-06:ancestor-active:ancestor-proof-06.jsonl",
    "ancestor-proof-07:ancestor-active:ancestor-proof-07.jsonl",
    "ancestor-proof-08:ancestor-active:ancestor-proof-08.jsonl"
  ],
  "lastTargets": [
    "ancestor-proof-33:ancestor-active:ancestor-proof-33.jsonl",
    "ancestor-proof-34:ancestor-active:ancestor-proof-34.jsonl",
    "current-proof-session:reset-archive:current-proof-session.jsonl.reset.2026-06-04T00-04-00.000Z",
    "current-proof-session:active:current-proof-session.jsonl"
  ],
  "currentResetTargetPresent": true,
  "currentActiveLast": true,
  "ancestor04Present": false,
  "ancestor34Present": true,
  "archiveHeavyTopicTargetCount": 0,
  "carryoverSummary": "Exact-head ba74ecd54e carryover 34",
  "carryoverTokensBefore": 2034,
  "promptRolesBeforeLlm": ["compactionSummary", "user"],
  "compactionSummaryCount": 1,
  "idempotentRoles": ["compactionSummary", "user"]
}
```

**Evidence after fix:**

- The shared resolver returned 32 targets and kept both current reset archive and current active transcript inside the cap.
- The current active transcript was ordered last for final history trimming.
- The old over-cap ancestor was not read: `ancestor04Present` is false.
- The newest eligible ancestor survived even though older retained ancestor 05 had 35 owned reset-topic archives: `ancestor34Present` is true and `archiveHeavyTopicTargetCount` is 0.
- Carryover selected the newest retained ancestor summary, `Exact-head ba74ecd54e carryover 34`, and preserved its token count.
- The embedded prompt transform injected exactly one `compactionSummary` before the model boundary and remained idempotent on a second pass.

## What Problem This Solves
It makes each published container release produce inspectable SBOM artifacts, uploads Trivy vulnerability findings into GitHub Code Scanning, and gates the release only on fixed critical vulnerabilities. It also covers both GHCR and Docker Hub images across amd64 and arm64, so the security evidence matches what users can actually pull.


## Why This Change Was Made
Generate SPDX and CycloneDX SBOM artifacts for released container images,
upload Trivy SARIF results to Code Scanning, and fail releases only on
critical vulnerabilities after all scan reports are produced.

Should be no impact but the goal is to increase security coverage

target.title: fix(chat): keep proof decision out of actor closure
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Swift 6.2 strict concurrency rejects `OpenClawChatSQLiteTranscriptCache.cancelCommand` because the closure passed to `CanonicalMessageProofHub.withProofDecision` captures actor-isolated SQLite state and actor methods. The failing diagnostic is `sending 'db' risks causing data races`, and it blocks `GatewayEndpointStoreTests`, the `OpenClaw` product build, and packaged app verification from current `main`.

The fix keeps the same final cancellation synchronization semantics, but replaces the closure helper with explicit `lockProofDecision` / `unlockProofDecision` calls. That keeps the final proof decision, SQLite commit, and cache removal inside the same synchronized region while leaving actor-isolated work in the actor method body.

## Summary

- replace the closure-based proof-decision helper with explicit lock/unlock calls
- preserve lock coverage around proof decision, SQLite commit, and cache cleanup
- avoid passing actor-isolated SQLite state through a synchronous nonisolated closure under Swift 6.2

## Evidence

Validated on the rebased head `d3201ef67836cb9109419ff32d6b9908267696ff`:

- `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter ChatTranscriptCacheStoreTests` (39 tests passed)
- `swift test --package-path apps/macos --filter ChatTranscriptCacheIdentityTests` (6 tests passed)
- `swift test --package-path apps/macos --filter GatewayEndpointStoreTests` (33 tests passed)
- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --product OpenClaw`

target.title: [AI-assisted] Add session history family lookup
target.body:
## Problem

When a threaded conversation has already been split across reset transcripts, `chat.history` and the `sessions_history` tool only read the currently active transcript. The session store can already retain the family through `usageFamilySessionIds`, but history readers do not use that chain and do not discover archived `*.jsonl.reset.<timestamp>` topic transcripts.

That means an agent/tool can be looking at the correct logical Telegram/Slack/Discord thread and still miss earlier turns after session rollover.

## Fix

Add an opt-in family history path:

- `chat.history` accepts `includeFamily: true`.
- `sessions_history` accepts `includeFamily`.
- Gateway and embedded `chat.history` now share the bounded/header-checked reset archive resolver instead of using separate prefix scans.
- The shared resolver can include owned topic-suffixed reset archives such as `<sessionId>-topic-456.jsonl.reset.<timestamp>` only when the archive header matches the requested session id.
- Same-prefix colliding topic archives and headerless topic archives are ignored.
- Family read targets are capped before transcript reads, and normal `chat.history` behavior remains opt-in: UI startup does not load ancestor history.

## Validation

Current head: `1aa4e9cbb94f6841803bd55559aa0ea6de17dc67`.

target.title: [codex] Keep ambiguous delivery attempts recoverable
target.body:
## Summary

- Keeps outbound delivery entries in ambiguous post-send states pending when adapter reconciliation is unavailable.
- Preserves the existing no-blind-replay behavior while leaving the entry retryable for later reconciliation/backoff.
- Avoids consuming retry budget when no reconciliation-capable adapter ran, so ambiguous entries do not age into terminal failure before a later adapter can reconcile them.
- Treats a reconciliation-capable adapter returning `null` as a completed unresolved reconciliation attempt, so that path still consumes retry budget and respects the max-retry cap.
- Updates startup recovery, reconnect-drain, and outbound queue integration coverage plus Discord troubleshooting guidance for #87544.

## Scope

This is a narrow mitigation for #87544 and intentionally does not close the full issue. The broader transcript-to-provider delivery ledger, Discord reconciliation semantics, and UI/API surfacing still need maintainer design.

## Validation

- Automation main refresh (2026-07-08 JST / 2026-07-07 UTC): merged `openclaw/openclaw@623534400684eca7c451cf587189fae714f2abe2` into the PR branch. The merge conflicted in `src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-storage.ts` and `src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts`; resolved by keeping main's pre-connect send-evidence cleanup and this PR's no-budget reconciliation-deferral path/tests.
- Follow-up main refresh in the same run: `origin/main` advanced again to `7ff3f2dbf922d233bd8c86c6609f53185cf9f496`; merged it with no conflicts and pushed final head `22a8b2d41094862f98000e0dcdcf1b3791c2c23d`.
- GitHub pre-refresh state checked: PR was open/ready with head `1779a704bc1b3a9e7b57e994fea534fac68c2eec`, base `a7c4a0471d944e3c3bf2b3071a5b1b485548dc8d`, `mergeable=CONFLICTING` via GraphQL, and the local branch was 378 commits behind `origin/main`.
- GitHub post-refresh state checked: PR head is `22a8b2d41094862f98000e0dcdcf1b3791c2c23d`, base is `7ff3f2dbf922d233bd8c86c6609f53185cf9f496`; GitHub CI is pending on the refreshed head and `reviewDecision` remains empty/null.
- Review threads checked with GraphQL: 4 total, 0 unresolved. Existing connector reviews are `COMMENTED` only and are not treated as approval.
- `gh pr checks 87552 --repo openclaw/openclaw --required --json name,state,bucket,link,workflow`
  - GitHub reported no required checks on the PR branch.
- Current-head refresh validation:
  - `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
  - `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD`
  - `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD`
  - `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-storage.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.storage.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts src/infra/outbound/deliver.queue-integration.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts` was attempted locally after the conflicted merge, but the infra Vitest runner produced no test output for 150s and was interrupted; the narrower recovery-file run also produced no test output for 120s and was interrupted. Formatter/PR-diff checks passed locally; current-head GitHub CI is the active validation source.
  - Functional PR diff remains scoped to 7 files: 2 source, 4 tests, 1 docs; 293 insertions / 36 deletions.
- Current-head GitHub CI after push: pending on the new head, including Real behavior proof and normal CI/security guard buckets.
- Previous scoped validation for the functional changes, before this main refresh:
  - `node scripts/docs-list.js`
  - `node scripts/generate-docs-map.mjs --check`
  - `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-storage.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-recovery.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.storage.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts src/infra/outbound/deliver.queue-integration.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts docs/channels/troubleshooting.md`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.storage.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts src/infra/outbound/deliver.queue-integration.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts`
    - 4 files passed, 69 tests passed.
  - `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main`
    - Clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: ambiguous outbound delivery entries whose platform send may have started must not be blindly replayed, and must remain pending/recoverable without consuming retry budget when adapter reconciliation is unavailable.

Real environment tested: local OpenClaw source checkout on macOS with Node v22.22.3, rebased onto `openclaw/openclaw@c5d34c8376f8aa32744786cae0473c60e39ef444`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: ran a one-off `node --import tsx --input-type=module` terminal proof that invoked the real `enqueueDelivery`, `markDeliveryPlatformOutcomeUnknown`, `recoverPendingDeliveries`, `loadPendingDeliveries`, and SQLite state reader against a temporary OpenClaw state directory. The proof queued an `unknown_after_send` outbound entry, ran recovery with no reconciliation-capable adapter, and failed if `deliver` was called, the entry did not remain pending, or retry budget was consumed.

Evidence after fix:

```text
info: Found 1 pending delivery entries — starting recovery
warn: Delivery entry <redacted-queue-id> delivery state is unknown_after_send; refusing blind replay without adapter reconciliation
warn: Retry failed for delivery <redacted-queue-id>: delivery state is unknown_after_send; refusing blind replay without adapter reconciliation
info: Delivery recovery complete: 0 recovered, 1 failed, 0 skipped (max retries), 0 deferred (backoff)
proof summary: {"recovered":0,"failed":1,"skippedMaxRetries":0,"deferredBackoff":0}
deliver call count: 0
pending entries: 1
queue row: {"status":"pending","retry_count":0,"recovery_state":"unknown_after_send","last_error":"delivery state is unknown_after_send; refusing blind replay without adapter reconciliation"}
```

Observed result after fix: recovery refused blind replay, did not call the delivery function, kept exactly one pending queue entry, and persisted `status: "pending"`, `retry_count: 0`, and `recovery_state: "unknown_after_send"`.

What was not tested: no live Discord gateway/channel send was performed in this pass. The broader transcript-to-provider delivery ledger, Discord reconciliation semantics, and Control UI/API delivery-state surface remain open under #87544.

Problem

OpenClaw can surface HTTP 530 from the provider/CDN path as a terminal error instead of a fallback-triggering transient timeout. That blocks model failover in the same class of temporary upstream outages that already fall back for 499/500/502/503/504/521/522/523/524/529.

- The model-failover docs describe fallback for transient provider failures; 530 is the missing edge in that path.

Fix

- Treat 530 as transient/timeout in the failover classifier.
- Add regression coverage for structured `status: 530` and provider-runtime classification.

## What Problem This Solves

`web_fetch` can currently reach any public hostname that passes the core SSRF checks. Enterprises that need default-deny egress therefore have to rely entirely on an external proxy or network overlay, and a permissive cached response or hosted-provider fallback must not bypass a tighter runtime policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add optional `tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy.hostnameAllowlist` entries for exact hostnames and subdomain-only wildcards such as `*.example.com`.
- Normalize and validate patterns, rejecting blank, malformed, and catch-all values.
- Enforce the policy on initial requests, redirects, trusted-proxy dispatch, and cache hits through the existing SSRF matcher.
- Include the effective policy in cache keys and suppress hosted-provider fallback while a hostname restriction is active.
- Keep the new hostname restriction scoped to `web_fetch`; remote media paths receive only the two existing fake-IP compatibility flags.
- Preserve the existing sanitized security audit warning for blocked initial URLs.

## User Impact

Operators can opt into an application-level egress allowlist for `web_fetch` while retaining OpenClaw's DNS/IP SSRF defenses and external network controls. Existing configurations are unchanged when the option is unset. Exact entries match only that host; `*.example.com` matches subdomains but not the apex.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(feishu): replace longer mention keys first
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes Feishu inbound mention normalization when mention keys share prefixes, such as `@_user_1`, `@_user_10`, and `@_user_11`.

Feishu sends the stable mention identity in `message.mentions`; the text body only contains per-message placeholder keys. The previous replacement loop processed keys in event order, so replacing `@_user_1` first could rewrite the prefix inside `@_user_10` and prevent the longer key from ever resolving.

This patch keeps the existing source-of-truth behavior from `mentions`, but replaces longer keys first. That fixes the prefix collision without adding a delimiter rule, so adjacent text like `@_user_1thanks` still normalizes the listed mention and preserves the suffix.

Supersedes the approach in #96284.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/bot-content.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/bot.stripBotMention.test.ts`
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --parallel-tests "node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/bot-content.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/bot.stripBotMention.test.ts"`

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Feishu mention placeholders with shared prefixes are normalized to the wrong user when a shorter key is replaced before a longer key.

Real environment tested: local Vitest through the repo `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` wrapper.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/bot-content.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/bot.stripBotMention.test.ts
```

Evidence after fix:

```text
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests  13 passed (13)
```

Observed result after fix: `@_user_10` and `@_user_11` resolve to their own users even when `@_user_1` is also present, and `@_user_1thanks` still normalizes the listed mention while preserving `thanks`.

What was not tested: live Feishu group round-trip; the patch covers the pure normalization function used by `parseFeishuMessageEvent`.

target.title: feat: add agent-scoped exec environments
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Specialized agents currently share the Gateway process environment. Giving one agent a scoped API credential therefore requires process-wide env, wrapper scripts, or a separate deployment, and host exec can inherit unrelated Gateway credentials by default.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add agent-only `agents.list[].tools.exec.env` values with SecretRef support.
- Add `inheritHostEnv: false` for a minimal Gateway exec environment and disable shell-startup snapshots in that mode.
- Keep precedence deterministic: model env < agent env < trusted plugin env < trusted channel context.
- Bind approval metadata to env keys without serializing Gateway credential values.
- Reject configured agent env for node-host exec before remote preparation; node credentials must be configured on the node.
- Redact the wildcard env surface in config snapshots and expose its full SecretInput shape in generated config schema.
- Preserve POSIX case-sensitive inherited/sandbox env semantics while applying case-folded precedence only when an override targets a key.

## User Impact

Operators can give a specialized agent its own exec-only credentials without adding them to every Gateway child process. Setting `inheritHostEnv: false` further limits ambient credential inheritance. Existing behavior remains the default, and node-host deployments continue to configure credentials on the node itself.

This scopes subprocess injection; it is not a same-process plugin or same-OS-user security boundary. Any command available to the agent can read the configured values.

## Evidence

- Focused agent/config/SecretRef/security suites pass, including agent isolation, approval metadata, schema lookup, redaction, case precedence, stale channel context, node rejection, and inactive node-only SecretRefs.
- Gateway env-binding approval cases pass.
- Base config schema, config docs baseline, plugin SDK API baseline, docs MDX, docs links, formatting, lint, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent security/API review is clean after fixes.
- Repository autoreview rerun after all findings were addressed.

target.title: [codex] Confirm Telegram final delivery before completion
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram final replies can currently be treated as completed when OpenClaw has only queued or attempted the final reply, rather than evidence that Telegram accepted and delivered a visible message. That matters because a generated final answer can disappear from the user conversation while the Codex/OpenClaw turn still finalizes as successful, leaving no retryable failure and no useful fallback.

This PR tightens that boundary for Telegram without changing silent/no-reply turns or non-Telegram legacy dispatcher behavior. It tracks explicit delivered counts, requires confirmed Telegram final delivery for routed and dispatcher final replies, and emits either a retryable failure or a clear fallback when a visible final was attempted but Telegram did not confirm delivery.

## Summary

- Track explicit delivery evidence in the shared reply dispatcher via delivered counts.
- Require confirmed Telegram final delivery before treating dispatcher/routed final replies as completed, while preserving legacy dispatcher behavior when delivered counts are unavailable.
- Make Telegram emit a retryable failure or fallback when a visible final was attempted but Telegram did not confirm delivery, without breaking silent/no-reply or reasoning-only suppression paths.
- Gate `attemptedVisibleFinalDelivery` on actual normalized visible send attempts: routed replies now report `attemptedDelivery` only after durable delivery returns a non-suppressed send result, and dispatcher finals report a visible attempt only when the normalized final was queued.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the real failure class locally from Telegram delivery history: a final reply was generated but Telegram delivery failed, while the surrounding turn still risked looking complete from the agent side.
- Added focused dispatcher coverage for explicit delivery evidence: `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-dispatcher.ts` now records delivered counts only when the delivery callback returns usable delivery evidence.
- Added routed/final outcome coverage in `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.final-outcome-counts.test.ts` and `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-flow.test.ts`.
- Added Telegram behavior coverage in `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.test.ts` for unconfirmed final delivery fallback and retryable failure when fallback is suppressed.
- Added ClawSweeper follow-up coverage:
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/route-reply.test.ts`: silent/empty routed payloads do not report `attemptedDelivery`; visible routed payloads do.
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts`: exact `NO_REPLY` and whitespace-only finals do not set `attemptedVisibleFinalDelivery` and do not call delivery.
  - `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.test.ts`: normalized `NO_REPLY` and empty final turns stay silent when no visible final was attempted, while the existing unconfirmed visible-final tests still produce exactly one fallback or retryable failure.
- Added ClawSweeper hook-suppression follow-up coverage:
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/route-reply.ts`: `attemptedDelivery` is set only after the durable send result is known and not suppressed.
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/route-reply.test.ts`: cancelled and emptied reply-payload hook suppression now explicitly assert no `attemptedDelivery`.
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts`: routed Telegram finals suppressed by reply-payload hooks do not set `attemptedVisibleFinalDelivery`.

## Redacted Behavior Proof

Focused after-fix proof was rerun locally after rebasing onto current `main` (`a2725b6a24`) against PR head `2ec5ad5f8a`:


The proof is intentionally redacted to local file paths and aggregate test output. The covered behavior is the Telegram-visible outcome ClawSweeper flagged: missing confirmed visible final delivery still creates the fallback/retry path, while intentional `NO_REPLY`, empty finals, and reply-payload hook-suppressed routed finals do not create a visible fallback.

﻿Closes #101837

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `web_fetch` could see a response reported as truncated when the streamed response body was exactly `maxResponseBytes` bytes, even though no bytes were omitted.

## Why This Change Was Made

`readResponseText` now treats truncation as proven only when a chunk exceeds the remaining byte budget. Reaching the byte budget exactly no longer flips the truncation flag by itself, so exact-limit responses can complete normally while true overflow still cancels the reader.

## User Impact

Users no longer get misleading `Response body truncated after ... bytes.` warnings for complete responses that happen to land exactly on the byte cap. Oversized responses are still bounded and marked truncated.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: Current head `18b610b93e7e0a96de0eb891de3bab0e43f2c74b` lets an exact-limit `readResponseText` helper run complete without setting `truncated`, while still reporting the exact byte count.
- Real helper proof for the requested boundary, constructing a real `Response` from streamed chunks `"hello"` + `" world"` and reading it with `maxBytes: 11`:
  ```text
  node --import ../openclaw/node_modules/tsx/dist/esm/index.mjs --input-type=module -e "import { readResponseText } from './src/agents/tools/web-shared.ts'; const encoder = new TextEncoder(); let cancelCount = 0; const response = new Response(new ReadableStream({ start(controller) { controller.enqueue(encoder.encode('hello')); controller.enqueue(encoder.encode(' world')); controller.close(); }, cancel() { cancelCount += 1; } })); const result = await readResponseText(response, { maxBytes: 11 }); console.log(JSON.stringify({ text: result.text, truncated: result.truncated, bytesRead: result.bytesRead, cancelCount }));"
  {"text":"hello world","truncated":false,"bytesRead":11,"cancelCount":0}
  ```
- Focused regression: `PNPM_CONFIG_MODULES_DIR='../openclaw/node_modules' node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/web-shared.test.ts` passed (`1` file, `12` tests).
- Whitespace check: `git diff --check` passed.
- GitHub current-head checks: `gh pr checks 101845 --repo openclaw/openclaw --json name,bucket,state,completedAt,link` showed no failed buckets; current checks are pass/skip/neutral.
- Duplicate search before issue creation: no open issue or PR found for `web_fetch truncated maxBytes exact limit` or `readResponseText truncated maxBytes`.

Observed result: exact-limit helper output is `truncated:false`, `bytesRead:11`, and `cancelCount:0`, so the shared helper no longer feeds a false truncation warning to `web_fetch` for complete exact-cap responses.

target.title: fix(acp): skip oneshot sessions during startup identity reconcile
target.body:
Fixes #72013

## Summary

Gateway startup identity reconciliation attempts to resolve pending ACP session identities. Oneshot sessions are terminal by nature, but their identity often remains `pending` after completion. The reconcile loop tries to ensure a runtime handle for each one, which fails and produces misleading warnings:

```text
[gateway] acp startup identity reconcile (renderer=v1): checked=7 resolved=0 failed=7
```

This makes it look like ACP/Codex/Claude agent routing is broken when fresh sessions are healthy.

## Fix

Skip sessions with `mode === "oneshot"` in `runManagerStartupIdentityReconcile` so the startup scan only processes persistent sessions that may genuinely need identity resolution.

## Changed files

- `src/acp/control-plane/manager.startup-identity-reconcile.ts` -- Added `session.acp.mode === "oneshot"` guard after the session key check
- `src/acp/control-plane/manager.startup-identity-reconcile.test.ts` -- Regression test: oneshot session with pending identity is skipped (checked=0, no ensure/getStatus calls)
- `scripts/prove-acp-startup-oneshot-list-visible.ts` -- Production-path proof: session-store-visible `listAcpSessionEntries` + reconcile eligibility

## Overlap with #85399

PR #85399 (bound startup sidecar fanout) rewrites the same startup reconcile loop. This PR's guard (`session.acp.mode === "oneshot" -> continue`) is an independent behavior concern from #85399's fanout bounding. Both changes apply cleanly on the same function. Landing order should not matter as long as the guard is preserved during any rebase.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Startup identity reconcile must not process store-visible oneshot ACP rows that still have pending identity + stable `acpxSessionId`, while persistent pending rows remain eligible.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS arm64, Node from workspace toolchain, OpenClaw PR branch `fix/acp-reconcile-skip-oneshot` at commit after proof script add, using **production** `listAcpSessionEntries` + `runManagerStartupIdentityReconcile` (not a reimplemented loop).
- **Why SQLite-only proof is insufficient:** `listAcpSessionEntries` joins SQLite `acp_sessions` rows to a readable session-store entry and **drops** rows without a matching store entry (`session-meta.ts`). This proof seeds **both** the JSON session store and SQLite via production `upsertAcpSessionMeta`, then prints direct list output.
- **Exact command run after this patch:**

```console
$ pnpm exec tsx scripts/prove-acp-startup-oneshot-list-visible.ts
```

- **Evidence (redacted paths are machine temp dirs; no secrets):**

```console
PROOF_DIR=/var/folders/7_/3g02szlx2h3_4pdqp0knlw740000gn/T/openclaw-86711-proof-yxDHaj
STORE_PATH=/var/folders/7_/3g02szlx2h3_4pdqp0knlw740000gn/T/openclaw-86711-proof-yxDHaj/sessions/main.json
DATABASE_PATH=/var/folders/7_/3g02szlx2h3_4pdqp0knlw740000gn/T/openclaw-86711-proof-yxDHaj/state/openclaw.sqlite
LIST_ACP_SESSION_ENTRIES_COUNT=2
LIST_ROW sessionKey=agent:main:acp:oneshot-proof-visible mode=oneshot state=idle identityState=pending hasAcpxSessionId=true storeSessionId=sess-oneshot-proof
LIST_ROW sessionKey=agent:main:acp:persistent-proof-visible mode=persistent state=idle identityState=pending hasAcpxSessionId=true storeSessionId=eeeedc2b-ead9-40e5-b40e-71fa768ecf19
ONESHOT_STORE_VISIBLE=true
PERSISTENT_STORE_VISIBLE=true
RECONCILE_ELIGIBLE_CALL sessionKey=agent:main:acp:persistent-proof-visible mode=persistent
RECONCILE_RESULT checked=1 resolved=0 failed=0
ENSURE_CALLS=["agent:main:acp:persistent-proof-visible"]
ONESHOT_ENSURE_SKIPPED=true
PERSISTENT_ENSURE_CALLED=true
PROOF_OK

```

Interpretation:
- `LIST_ACP_SESSION_ENTRIES_COUNT=2` with both `ONESHOT_STORE_VISIBLE=true` and `PERSISTENT_STORE_VISIBLE=true` shows the startup scan input path sees both rows (the ClawSweeper gap from SQLite-only injection).
- `RECONCILE_RESULT checked=1` with `ONESHOT_ENSURE_SKIPPED=true` and `PERSISTENT_ENSURE_CALLED=true` shows oneshot is skipped while the persistent pending stable row remains reconcile-eligible.

target.title: fix(plugins): bound hosted catalog feed reads on non-streaming responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readHostedCatalogResponseText` in `src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.ts` used two read paths: the streaming branch incrementally enforced `maxBytes`, but the non-streaming branch called `response.text()` first and only checked the byte count afterward. That check-after-allocate pattern could OOM on oversized bodies when the response was not stream-backed or when `Content-Length` was missing or wrong.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route all hosted catalog feed reads through the shared `readResponseWithLimit` helper from `src/infra/http-body.ts`, reusing the same byte cap, idle timeout, and overflow error contract as other bounded HTTP reads. For stream-less fetch shapes, fail closed instead of trusting `Content-Length` before the shared helper's `arrayBuffer()` fallback. This deletes the duplicate streaming loop and the unsafe `response.text()` branch.

## User Impact

Normal hosted catalog loads are unchanged for stream-backed responses. Oversized feeds fail at the shared byte cap; stream-less feeds now fail closed with `hosted catalog feed streaming response body unavailable` instead of trusting `Content-Length` and risking a full-body allocation.

## Evidence

```bash
node --import tsx scripts/proof-hosted-catalog-bound.mjs
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Non-streaming hosted catalog feed reads could allocate the full response body before enforcing `maxBytes`; stream-less oversized bodies could still buffer via `arrayBuffer()` fallback.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS (Darwin), Node.js v22.22.0, `node:http` loopback server on `127.0.0.1`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  1. `node --import tsx scripts/proof-hosted-catalog-bound.mjs`
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose`
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-hosted-catalog-bound.mjs
  ok: unbounded read pulled the full oversized feed (1572963 bytes)
  ok: rejected oversized hosted catalog feed
  ok: bounded error message present
  ok: streamless hosted feed with underreported content-length is rejected
  ok: streamless hosted feed never reaches arrayBuffer()

ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS PASSED
```

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
 ✓ rejects non-streaming hosted feeds before buffering underreported bodies
 ✓ rejects oversized streaming hosted feeds incrementally
 ✓ rejects non-streaming hosted feeds without content-length

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  55 passed (55)
```

- **Observed result after fix:** `loadHostedOfficialExternalPluginCatalogEntries` rejects a ~1.5 MiB loopback feed at the 1 MiB cap with `hosted catalog feed exceeds 1048576 bytes`; stream-less responses are rejected with `hosted catalog feed streaming response body unavailable`; and the underreported `Content-Length` proof confirms that path never reaches `arrayBuffer()`.
- **What was not tested:** Live ClawHub hosted catalog endpoints; proof used loopback fetch and mocked `fetchImpl` only.

## Tests and validation

- `node --import tsx scripts/proof-hosted-catalog-bound.mjs` (committed on branch)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose`
- Regression tests added in `src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts`

## Risk checklist

- Did user-visible behavior change? Yes — oversized hosted feeds error at the cap on stream-backed responses; stream-less hosted feeds are now rejected.
- Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? No
- Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? Yes — hosted catalog feed reads now use one bounded HTTP reader and refuse stream-less remote responses.
- Highest-risk area: plugin catalog refresh / hosted feed fallback behavior on large but legitimate feeds.
- Mitigation: default cap remains 1 MiB; successful feeds are far below it; bundled fallback behavior is unchanged on overflow.

## AI-assisted disclosure

- [x] AI-assisted (Cursor agent)
- [x] Human-run Real behavior proof from local setup

## Problem When a user quote-replies to the bot's message in a Microsoft Teams 1:1 DM, the bot could not see the quoted message content — it only saw the user's new text. Root cause: Teams delivers the quoted text of a quote-reply inside `

…

` (a truncated snippet), but `extractMSTeamsQuoteInfo` only matched `

…

`. The match failed, `quoteInfo` came back `undefined`, and nothing was surfaced to the agent via `supplemental.quote`. ## Fix **1. Parser (primary):** `extractMSTeamsQuoteInfo` now matches `

` **or** `

` (prefers `copy`, falls back to `preview`), and captures the blockquote `itemid` as the quoted message id. Sender extraction (``) is unchanged. **2. Full text via Graph (enhancement):** the `preview` snippet is Teams-truncated, so when the quoted message id is known we fetch the complete text via the app-only endpoint `GET /chats/{chatId}/messages/{id}` (permitted with the `Chat.Read.All` application permission, unlike the delegated `/me/chats` listing) and use it as the quote body. Scoped to non-channel chats (DM + group) whose Graph chat id is a `19:` id — channel quote context is already covered by the thread-parent path. Wrapped in try/catch; **any failure degrades to the truncated preview from fix 1**, so message handling never breaks. ## Notes / limitations - For 1:1 DMs the Graph chat id is the synthesized `19:{aadObjectId}_{appId}@unq.gbl.spaces` (the fork already computes this for media). This has not been exhaustively verified as accepted by the message-fetch endpoint against every tenant; the graceful fallback ensures correctness regardless. A local `messageId → text` cache (extending `sent-message-cache.ts`) is a robust alternative if the synthesized id proves unreliable. - The delegated `resolveGraphChatId` path is untouched (still used elsewhere). ## Testing - `extensions/msteams/src/inbound.test.ts` — added tests for `preview`-only parsing, `copy`-preferred-over-`preview`, `itemid` capture, and a full real-payload case. - `extensions/msteams/src/graph-thread.test.ts` — added tests for the new `fetchChatMessageText` helper (HTML stripping + path, non-HTML trim, error → undefined, no-body → undefined). - Vitest (msteams): inbound + graph-thread suites pass (58 tests); message-handler suites pass (40 tests). - `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` both pass with no errors. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Closes #101810

AI-assisted with Codex.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Android chat link previews could keep background network work alive after the preview coroutine was cancelled, such as when users scroll away from a preview or leave the chat screen while metadata or image fetches are still in flight.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Android link preview fetcher now awaits OkHttp responses through a cancellable coroutine bridge that maps coroutine cancellation to `Call.cancel()`. target.title: fix(feishu): keep full streamed answer when final payload is only the last block
target.body:
## Problem

With a streaming card enabled (`channels.feishu.*.streaming: true`), multi-message replies render correctly **while streaming**, but the **final message overwrites the whole streamed answer** — the card ends up showing only the last block.

Repro: a reply that emits one assistant message per tool round (e.g. a CLI/agent backend streaming "step 1/10 ✅ … step 10/10 ✅ done" across sleeps/tool calls). The card builds up the full answer live, then collapses to just `step 10/10 ✅ done` at finalization.

## Root cause

In `extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.ts`, the `info.kind === "final"` branch did `streamText = text` unconditionally. Normally `text` is the complete reply (a cumulative snapshot, or an answer already concatenated with a trailing notice), so replacing is correct. But when a backend emits one assistant message per tool round, the final payload is only the **last block** — already a subset of what was streamed — so replacing collapses the card to that block and drops everything before it.

## Fix

Keep the accumulated streamed text when the final payload is already contained in it; otherwise preserve the existing replace behavior:

```ts
streamText = text && streamText.includes(text) ? streamText : text;
```

## Validation

- New regression test in `reply-dispatcher.test.ts`: when the final payload is only the last block, the streaming card keeps the full accumulated answer.
- All existing `reply-dispatcher` tests pass (covers cumulative-final coalescing, answer+error finals, and error-final-replaces-transient-preview), so the replace behavior for those cases is unchanged.
- Verified end-to-end on a live Feishu deployment: a 10-step "report progress every interval" streaming reply now keeps the full content at finalization instead of collapsing to the last step.

Related to the Feishu streaming-card content-loss reports (#10078 final shows only the tail; #38824 / #38943 streaming-card content issues).

target.title: fix(exec-approval): distinguish non-persistable command from ask=always policy in approval prompt
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When \`allowAlwaysPersistence.kind === "one-shot"\` (for example, a command that uses shell redirection), \`allow-always\` is correctly excluded from the allowed decisions. The approval prompt still showed the same explanation used for an \`ask=always\` policy:

> "The effective approval policy requires approval every time, so Allow Always is unavailable."

That is misleading because the command can be approved; it just cannot be saved as a reusable approval pattern.

Closes #97069

## What Changed

1. **`exec-approval-reply.ts`** — added optional `nonPersistableCommand` field to `ExecApprovalPendingReplyParams`. When true, `buildExecApprovalPendingReplyPayload` emits a distinct message explaining the command cannot be saved as a reusable pattern.

2. **`bash-tools.exec-runtime.ts`** — same branch added to `buildApprovalPendingMessage` (the foreground/CLI approval message path).

3. **`bash-tools.exec-types.ts`** — added `nonPersistableCommand?: boolean` to the `approval-pending` variant of `ExecToolDetails`, so the flag survives the gateway→tool-result→embedded-handler hop.

4. **`bash-tools.exec-host-shared.ts`** — `buildExecApprovalPendingToolResult` accepts and passes `nonPersistableCommand` through to both the message builder and the details output.

5. **`bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.ts`** — derives and passes `nonPersistableCommand: effectiveAllowAlwaysPersistence.kind === "one-shot" && hostAsk !== "always"` to the tool-result builder.

6. **`bash-tools.exec-host-node.ts`** — same derivation using `allowAlwaysPersistence` and `approvalDecisionAsk`.

7. **`embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.ts`** — reads `nonPersistableCommand` from the pending details and forwards it to `buildExecApprovalPendingReplyPayload`.

8. **`exec-approval-forwarding.ts` (Telegram)** — derives `nonPersistableCommand` from `allowedDecisions` and `request.request.ask` and passes it through.

## Real Behavior Proof

**Unit tests — 188 passing across 5 test files:**

```
$ pnpm exec vitest run src/infra/exec-approval-reply.test.ts \
    src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-shared.test.ts \
    src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts

 Test Files  5 passed (5)
      Tests  188 passed (188)
   Duration  ~14s
```

**Specific non-persistable vs. policy tests in `exec-approval-reply.test.ts` (34/34):**
- `shows non-persistable message when allow-always is excluded by command type` — asserts message contains `"cannot be saved as a reusable pattern"`, not `"policy requires approval every time"`
- `shows policy message when allow-always is excluded by ask=always policy` — asserts message contains `"policy requires approval every time"`, not `"cannot be saved as a reusable pattern"`

**Gateway test — wiring verified at `buildExecApprovalPendingToolResult` call site:**
`src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts` — 106/106 passing, including tests that verify the pending tool result shape under various allowlist/ask configurations.

## Production Paths Now Wired

| Path | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Gateway foreground (`buildApprovalPendingMessage`) | always policy copy | ✅ correct copy |
| Gateway tool result details (`ExecToolDetails`) | no flag | ✅ flag stored |
| Embedded handler → reply payload | no flag | ✅ flag forwarded |
| Telegram forwarder → reply payload | no flag | ✅ flag derived + forwarded |
| Node foreground | always policy copy | ✅ correct copy |

target.title: fix(agents): avoid false unscheduled note after shell cron add
target.body:
Closes #52972

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who schedule reminders through a shell-driven `openclaw cron add ...` command could still receive the false note saying no reminder was scheduled in the turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reminder guard already trusts successful structured `cron` tool adds. This extends the same producer-side counter to successful `exec` and `bash` commands that run `openclaw cron add` and return a cron add response shaped like the CLI output.

The repair also handles the CLI warning path where `openclaw cron add --message ...` emits the missing-agent warning on stderr while still printing the successful JSON receipt on stdout. Exec aggregates stdout and stderr, so the parser now scans the aggregate for a valid cron-add JSON receipt instead of requiring the whole aggregate to be pure JSON. Failed commands and unrelated cron commands are ignored.

## User Impact

Users no longer get a contradictory unscheduled-reminder note after a shell cron add succeeds, including the default-agent warning case. Failed or unrelated shell commands still leave the guard active.

## Evidence

Redacted behavior proof, run from the PR checkout after rebasing on current `main`:

```text
aggregateContainsWarning=true
aggregateContainsJsonReceipt=true
```

target.title: fix(session-memory): bound session transcript reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`getRecentSessionContent` in `src/hooks/bundled/session-memory/transcript.ts` reads session transcript JSONL files with an unbounded `fs.promises.readFile` call. A runaway or corrupted session file could force the session-memory extraction path to buffer the entire file into memory, leading to OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

Session-memory extraction now uses a bounded hybrid reader:
- For transcripts that fit under the 16 MiB cap, it streams lines newest-first through the shared `streamSessionTranscriptLinesReverse` helper and stops before retaining a line that would cross the cap.
- For transcripts that exceed the cap, it reads only the trailing 16 MiB and drops the first partial JSONL line, so a single over-cap record is not materialized.

This avoids whole-file buffering while preserving recent session context.

## User Impact

Session-memory extraction now safely bounds oversized transcripts while still keeping the most recent messages available for context.

## Evidence

- Added regression tests covering:
  - a transcript exceeding the cap with recent trailing messages — asserts the recent messages are preserved and the huge early message is absent,
  - a single JSONL row larger than the cap — asserts `getRecentSessionContent` returns `null`.
- Local focused run: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/hooks/bundled/session-memory/transcript.test.ts --run` passes (5/5 tests).

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

I ran a standalone Node script outside Vitest that imports the actual changed helper from source and exercises both the oversized-tail path and the lone over-cap row path.

target.title: add per-conversation whatsapp debounce config
target.body:
## Summary

Adds per-conversation inbound debounce configuration for WhatsApp direct chats and groups.

Practically, this controls how long OpenClaw waits before starting an agent turn after receiving a WhatsApp message from a specific conversation. This is useful when a contact sends multiple messages in a row: OpenClaw can wait a few seconds or minutes, collect the full burst, and then let the agent process the conversation with better context.

## What Problem This Solves

The existing WhatsApp debounce setting is too broad for mixed usage.

Some conversations should be processed immediately, while others should wait briefly:

- owner/admin chats often need immediate processing, so they can use `debounceMs: 0`
- external contacts often send multiple short messages in a row, so they can use a longer debounce, such as `180000`, to wait 3 minutes
- noisy groups can have their own debounce window
- wildcard entries can define defaults for all direct chats or all groups

This lets operators tune batching by conversation without changing the global WhatsApp debounce for every chat.

## Behavior

- supports `debounceMs` in `channels.whatsapp.direct`
- supports `debounceMs` in `channels.whatsapp.groups`
- supports wildcard entries like `direct["*"]` and `groups["*"]`
- specific conversation config wins over wildcard config
- falls back to the existing global WhatsApp debounce when no conversation override exists
- `debounceMs: 0` disables debounce for that conversation only

## Evidence

Redacted real WhatsApp setup proof from a local OpenClaw home:

The run used the PR branch plus real WhatsApp session keys from the local OpenClaw session index. The proof output prints only counts and redacted aliases; it does not include phone numbers, group JIDs, contact names, credentials, or message bodies. It feeds those real direct/group session keys through the same keyed inbound debouncer that the WhatsApp listener calls through `resolveDebounceMs`.


target.title: fix(matrix): tolerate SAS accept events missing method
target.body:
Closes #96188

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Matrix users could get stuck during SAS verification when Element sends an encrypted `m.key.verification.accept` to-device event without a `method` field. In that shape, matrix-js-sdk's Rust crypto preprocessing rejects the event before the Matrix plugin can continue the verification flow.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Matrix client now installs a narrow compatibility wrapper after `initRustCrypto()` that normalizes only `m.key.verification.accept` to-device events with missing or blank `content.method` to the SAS method (`m.sas.v1`) before Rust crypto preprocesses them. Existing methods, unrelated events, and the original event objects are left untouched.

This is intentionally scoped to the matrix-js-sdk Rust crypto preprocessor boundary because `/sync` to-device events reach Rust crypto before higher-level JS `MatrixEvent` compatibility hooks can run.

## User Impact

Matrix SAS verification with Element can continue instead of stalling on an opaque missing-field crypto error. There are no config, setup, or API changes.

## Evidence

- Rechecked live issue state: #96188 is open, and `gh pr list --repo openclaw/openclaw --state open --search "96188"` returned no superseding open PRs.
- Checked dependency behavior in local `matrix-js-sdk` source: `/sync` to-device events are sent through `cryptoCallbacks.preprocessToDeviceMessages()`, and the Rust crypto backend calls `receiveSyncChanges()` before JS compatibility events are emitted.
- Checked the current Matrix client-server spec for `m.key.verification.accept`; the SAS accept example carries `method: "m.sas.v1"`.

PR #93731 was closed because it subscribed to `message_reaction_count` updates without a runtime handler. That would let polling/webhook accept count updates and then silently drop them. This patch pairs the subscription with explicit aggregate-count handling, routing, docs, and tests.

## Behavior
- `message_reaction` still handles per-user reaction additions.
- `message_reaction_count` now emits events like `Telegram reaction counts changed: 👍 x3, 🔥 x2 on msg 42`.
- Aggregate count updates have no actor identity, so OpenClaw treats them as chat-level group events. Private chats are skipped, and sender-only allowlists do not authorize anonymous aggregate counts.
- Forum group count updates route to the general-topic session, matching existing reaction routing where Telegram omits thread IDs.

> [!NOTE]
> **AI-Assisted Contribution:** This PR was prepared and validated with the assistance of an AI coding assistant (Antigravity/Gemini).

## What Problem This Solves
Resolves a problem where the model auth subsystem ignores explicit `apiKey` (literal or SecretRef) overrides in `models.json` if store profiles exist (pr #100839).

1. Unless `auth: "api-key"` is explicitly set (making `shouldPreferExplicitConfigApiKeyAuth` true), the literal key or SecretRef configured in `models.json` is ignored during the binding phase (falling through `providerEntryBinding` checks). 3. In `models status` and `models auth list` commands, placeholder/marker values in the environment (e.g. `GOOGLE_API_KEY`) were treated as literal keys, causing incorrect `effective=models.json` formatting instead of falling back to store profiles.

target.title: fix(tool-search): normalize flattened target-tool args for tool_call
target.body:
Fixes #96115

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where local models (e.g., vLLM/Qwen) with `agents.defaults.experimental.localModelLean: true` drop target-tool arguments when calling `tool_call` through the compact Tool Search surface. The models emit target-tool parameters (such as `command`, `path`, `task`) flattened at the top level of `tool_call` alongside `id`, rather than nesting them under `args`. This causes the target tool to receive `{}` empty arguments and repeatedly fail with `missing required parameter` errors, creating a sticky failure loop.

## Why This Change Was Made

`readCallArgs` (`src/agents/tool-search.ts:1680`) only checked `params.args` and `params.input`, returning `{}` when neither was present. Local models are less precise at schema compliance than GPT/Claude and tend to place target-tool arguments at the top level next to `id`. The fix adds a flattened fallback without breaking the existing `args` nesting contract: when both `args` and `input` are absent, collect every top-level key except `id` from `params` and pass it as the target tool's `input`.

## User Impact

Users running local models with `localModelLean: true` can now invoke tools correctly without losing arguments. Users who explicitly nest arguments under `args` are unaffected.

## Evidence

**Environment**: Linux, Node v22.23.0, pnpm v11.2.2, worktree SHA 2af06042c2

**Before fix** (new regression test on old code):

```bash
$ pnpm test src/agents/tool-search.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

target.title: feat: render inline web chat widgets via capability-gated show_widget tool
target.body:
Closes #101790

## What Problem This Solves

Agents in the web chat can only answer in text and markdown. For content that is inherently visual — flow diagrams, small dashboards, comparisons, interactive explainers — a rendered inline widget communicates far better, and OpenClaw already ships the rendering substrate (the Canvas plugin's sandboxed embed pipeline). What was missing is a first-class tool for "render this markup inline in the chat transcript," and the underlying capability such a tool needs: a way to offer a tool only where the user's client can actually render its output. Today every gateway client (web UI, iOS, Android, macOS, CLI) collapses to the same internal message channel at tool-assembly time, so a web-only tool would have appeared — and dead-ended — on phones and terminals too.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two parts, deliberately layered:

**Client-capability-gated tool availability (generic core seam).** Gateway clients already declare capability flags at connect (`GATEWAY_CLIENT_CAPS`, previously only `tool-events`). This adds an `inline-widgets` capability that the browser Control UI declares, stamps the connected client's caps into the per-run message context at `chat.send` dispatch (mirroring `GatewayClientScopes`), and threads them through the run/queue/compaction paths into tool assembly. Tools — core or plugin — can declare `requiredClientCaps`; `createOpenClawTools` drops any tool whose required caps the originating client did not declare. Channel runs (Telegram, WhatsApp, …) have no gateway client and therefore no caps, so gated tools are simply absent there, and `tools.allow` cannot resurrect them (capability is a hard availability fact, not policy). Queue collect-mode batching keys on caps so runs from different surfaces don't merge. Additive protocol only: one new capability string, no version bump, no new config keys.

**`show_widget` tool (Canvas plugin).** The agent passes a `title` plus `widget_code` (`<svg …>` or an HTML fragment, ≤256 KiB). The plugin wraps it in a minimal HTML shell and persists it through the existing Canvas document store — bounded to 32 documents per session scope, oldest evicted — and returns the canvas preview handle the web chat already knows how to render, so the widget appears inline from the tool call itself and survives history reload with zero new UI rendering machinery.

**Security model** (hardened through two structured-review cycles):
- Widget iframes never get `allow-same-origin`: the preview carries a sandbox ceiling that caps the operator's global `embedSandbox` mode, enforced on both the inline preview and the sidebar open path.
- The Canvas host serves widget documents with a `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox allow-scripts` response header, so navigating to the hosted URL directly also runs the widget in an opaque origin rather than the Control UI origin.
- The widget document's own CSP (`default-src 'none'`; inline style/script; `data:` images) blocks external fetches and resource loads; the Control UI page CSP (`default-src 'self'`, no `frame-src`) additionally restricts where embedded frames can navigate. Scripts remain allowed by design — widgets are interactive — with the residual self-navigation limitation documented on the docs page.

## User Impact

Agents talking to the web Control UI gain a `show_widget` tool and can answer with rendered, optionally interactive, self-contained widgets inline in the chat. Users on Telegram, WhatsApp, the CLI, or the native apps see no change: the tool does not exist for those runs, so agents cannot call it into a void. Plugin authors get a documented, generic way to ship surface-conditional tools (`requiredClientCaps`), and native apps can adopt the widget surface later by declaring the capability. No configuration changes are required; the existing `gateway.controlUi.embedSandbox` tiers keep applying, with widgets capped below `trusted`.

## Evidence

- Capability gating: `src/agents/openclaw-tools.client-caps.test.ts` (absent caps exclude, superset includes, channel runs exclude, `tools.allow` cannot resurrect), `src/auto-reply/reply/queue/drain.client-caps.test.ts` (collect-mode batching keys on caps), `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.directive-tags.test.ts` (ctx stamping; 270 tests), `src/plugins/tool-descriptor-cache.test.ts` (caps survive descriptor caching).
- Widget tool: `extensions/canvas/src/widget-tool.test.ts` (validation, SVG/HTML wrapping with CSP meta, opaque ids, per-scope eviction, manifest sandbox marker), `extensions/canvas/src/host/server.test.ts` (sandbox-marked documents get the CSP sandbox header and skip live reload; unmarked documents unchanged).
- Web UI: `ui/src/api/gateway.node.test.ts` (Control UI declares `inline-widgets`), `ui/src/lib/chat/tool-display.node.test.ts` (sandbox ceiling math), `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-tool-cards.node.test.ts` (canvas handle extraction incl. sandbox; sidebar conversion preserves the ceiling), `ui/src/lib/chat/message-normalizer.test.ts`.
- `pnpm build` green with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]`; docs map/MDX/link checks green; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files; `git diff --check` clean.
- Structured autoreview ran until clean: two P1 findings surfaced and were fixed with regression tests (sidebar path dropping the sandbox ceiling under `trusted` mode; hosted widget documents executing as the app origin when opened directly), final review reported no actionable findings.
- Focused proof ran locally (hosted CI verifies the full gates at the exact head); remote box warmups were queued at the time, noted per validation policy.
